solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Critical CERN act resolved — this’ll go round the globe (9,6)

indicatorNotes.resolved: a problem resolved is broken down and worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

annotation.surface: Scientists at CERN resolve a critical experiment whose effects will be felt worldwide.
annotation.walkthrough: The dash makes the definition a whole phrase: a line of latitude really does go right round the globe.
annotation.definitionFit: The Antarctic Circle is a line of latitude encircling the Earth near the South Pole.

entries.clue: Fully expert English PhD, claims local fake (3-12)

indicatorNotes.fake: a fake is a made-up version, so the letters are made into something else

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
anagram fodder, taken letter for letter

annotation.surface: A local man boasts of an English doctorate that turns out to be bogus.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fully expert' reads as praise for the PhD holder, but it is the definition; 'fake' at the end sits after its fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone all-accomplished is skilled in every respect, that is, fully expert.

entries.clue: Retaliation from Italian stronghold in shelled state (3,3,3)

indicatorNotes.in: the Italian stronghold goes inside the state
indicatorNotes.shelled: a shelled nut loses its outer casing, so STATE loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: STATE without its outer letters
It is short for Italian vermouth
a fort is a stronghold

annotation.surface: A Mediterranean fortress is the base for revenge attacks within a battered country.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a war-torn country, but 'shelled' means stripped of its shell, like a nut. IT for Italian vermouth is a crossword convention.
annotation.definitionFit: Tit for tat is retaliation in kind, blow for blow.

entries.clue: Breach of trust at last entering clean sport after exchange (7)

indicatorNotes.at last: at last points to the final letter of 'at'
indicatorNotes.entering: entering means going in, so the T is put inside the word for clean
indicatorNotes.after exchange: clean and sport swap places, so RU comes before PURE

blocks.note: RU is rugby union
pure means clean
last letter of aT, placed after the P of PURE

annotation.surface: Trust is broken when a sport once thought clean turns out to be dirty.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'after exchange' as a doping scandal after a transfer; it is an instruction to swap the order of the two words before them. RU for rugby union is a crossword staple.
annotation.definitionFit: A rupture is a breach, as in a rupture of trust between two parties.

entries.clue: Unspoken diplomacy surrounding India (5)

indicatorNotes.surrounding: to surround something is to enclose it, so the word for diplomacy encloses the letter

blocks.note: tact is diplomacy
India is I in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Quiet diplomatic manoeuvring around India.
annotation.walkthrough: India is the NATO alphabet's word for I, not the country.
annotation.definitionFit: Tacit means understood without being spoken.

entries.clue: Clear the ground around wide part of vehicle (9)

indicatorNotes.ground: ground as in crushed, so the letters of CLEAR THE are broken up and reset
indicatorNotes.around: the rearranged letters go round W

blocks.note: anagram of CLEAR THE
W is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a wide

annotation.surface: Someone clears the land around a broad section of a vehicle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clear the ground' reads as one phrase about land, but 'ground' is the anagram instruction for CLEAR THE. A wide is a ball bowled out of the batter's reach in cricket.
annotation.definitionFit: A cartwheel is the wheel of a cart, so literally part of a vehicle.

entries.clue: Having no time at all, dump Rod’s port (7)

indicatorNotes.Having no time at all: every T (time) is taken out of the combined words

blocks.note: TIP (dump) without its T
SWITCH (a rod or cane) without its T

annotation.surface: In a hurry, Rod ditches his wine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'At all' matters: both TIP and SWITCH contain a T, and both must go. Ipswich is a port town in Suffolk, England.
annotation.definitionFit: Ipswich is a port on the River Orwell estuary in Suffolk.

entries.clue: Break Dave’s sidekick before Mike (5)

indicatorNotes.before: before means in front of, so the sidekick is written ahead of the letter for Mike

blocks.note: Chas and Dave were a London singing duo
Mike is M in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A friend's sidekick gets a break ahead of Mike.
annotation.walkthrough: Chas & Dave were a Cockney pub-rock duo from London, so Dave's partner is Chas.
annotation.definitionFit: A chasm is a deep break or gap, in rock or in relations.

entries.clue: Former US prison service voided a Conservative peer’s charge sheets? (7,8)

indicatorNotes.voided: service emptied of its middle leaves S and E

blocks.note: ex means former
pen is American slang for a penitentiary
the outer letters of SErvicE
taken as it stands
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a count is a peer, so peer's is COUNT'S

annotation.surface: An American prison service drops charges against a Tory lord.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charge sheets' sounds like police paperwork; the question mark flags a pun on charges as costs billed to an employer.
annotation.definitionFit: Expense accounts are records of costs charged to an employer, so sheets of charges.

entries.clue: Stop extremely loathsome set from the east (3,2)

indicatorNotes.extremely: only the extremes, first and last letters, of loathsome are used
indicatorNotes.from the east: in an across clue, read from the east means right to left

blocks.note: the outer letters of LoathsomE
to set something down is to put it

annotation.surface: A horrid group from the east is told to halt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Set' could be a noun, a group, which the surface wants; it is the verb, giving PUT.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal-verb synonym: rain that lets up stops, or at least eases off.

entries.clue: Second mouth organ found on witty guy who deals illegally? (4-5)

annotation.definitionNote: a relative clause standing for 'one who deals illegally', the noun the answer is

indicatorNotes.found on: in an across clue, one thing placed on another comes after it

blocks.note: a card is a witty or eccentric person
S is the abbreviation for second
a harp is slang for a harmonica, or mouth organ

annotation.surface: A comedian with a harmonica is suspected of dodgy dealing.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the pun on 'deals': a card-sharp deals cards dishonestly, not drugs.
annotation.definitionFit: A card-sharp cheats at cards, dealing illegally.

entries.clue: Game for abandoning cold blue cheese (7)

indicatorNotes.abandoning: the cheese abandons the letters FOR

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap
Roquefort is a French blue cheese
FOR is removed from ROQUEFORT, leaving ROQUET

annotation.surface: Someone gives up a cold blue cheese for a sport.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a link word between definition and wordplay, but it is the letters to be taken out.
annotation.definitionFit: Croquet is a lawn game played with mallets and hoops.

entries.clue: Jot piece for US poet (7)

blocks.note: a jot and a whit both mean a tiny amount
a man is a piece in chess or draughts

annotation.surface: Someone scribbles a short piece for an American poet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jot' is a noun here, not the verb 'write quickly', which is what the writing surface wants.
annotation.definitionFit: Walt Whitman was a nineteenth-century American poet, author of Leaves of Grass.

entries.clue: Mobile home agent working as a solicitor (2,3,4)

indicatorNotes.Mobile: mobile letters move about and rearrange

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: An estate agent selling mobile homes moonlights as a lawyer.
annotation.walkthrough: A solicitor is a British lawyer, which the surface wants, but here it is someone soliciting on the street; 'on the game' is British slang for working as a prostitute.
annotation.definitionFit: To be on the game is to work as a prostitute, one who solicits for clients.

entries.clue: Plant in Beirut, capital, regularly damaged (9)

indicatorNotes.regularly: every other letter of capital is taken
indicatorNotes.damaged: the letters are knocked out of shape and rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder
the even letters of cApItAl

annotation.surface: A plant in Beirut is damaged, as is the capital regularly.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital seems to be Beirut itself; it is the word 'capital' giving its alternate letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Aubrietia is a low trailing rock-garden plant with purple flowers.

entries.clue: Harbour almost brings in European haul (5)

indicatorNotes.almost: the harbour word is one letter short of complete
indicatorNotes.brings in: to bring something in is to take it inside, so the shortened harbour word holds the letter

blocks.note: HAVEN without its last letter
E is the abbreviation for European

annotation.surface: A port nearly takes in a European catch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Harbour' could be the verb, to shelter; it is the noun, a haven.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: sailors heave on a rope and haul on it alike, pulling with effort.

entries.clue: I draw Romeo, nailed by a dry performer (9)

annotation.definitionNote: the answer speaks for itself: an attractor could say 'I draw', so the verb phrase defines the noun

indicatorNotes.nailed by: R is fixed in place, pinned between the parts of a dry performer

blocks.note: taken as it stands
TT is teetotal, off the drink
Romeo is R in the phonetic alphabet
an actor is a performer

annotation.surface: A sober actor lands the part of Romeo, and the playwright says 'I draw' the crowds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I draw' is the definition in the first person: what an attractor would say of itself.
annotation.definitionFit: An attractor is something that draws or pulls things toward it.

entries.clue: Excessive work held back primate (5)

indicatorNotes.held back: held back means turned backwards, so OTT + OP reads right to left

blocks.note: OTT is over the top
op is short for opus, a work

annotation.surface: Excess work held back a monkey.
annotation.walkthrough: A potto is a slow-moving African primate.
annotation.definitionFit: The potto is a small nocturnal primate of African forests.

entries.clue: Old wild ass pulled up herb (7)

indicatorNotes.pulled up: in a down clue, pulled up means reading upward

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
an onager is an Asian wild ass

annotation.surface: An old wild donkey is pulled up by the herb patch.
annotation.walkthrough: The onager is a crossword favourite for wild ass.
annotation.definitionFit: Oregano is a culinary herb of the mint family.

entries.clue: Projectile is following line into sea (9)

indicatorNotes.following: following means coming behind, so 'is' is written after the letter for line
indicatorNotes.into: into means going inside, so that pair is put within the sea

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for line
taken as it stands
the Baltic Sea

annotation.surface: A missile is launched along a line into the sea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Projectile' looks like a noun, a missile; it is the adjective, meaning thrown or propelled.
annotation.definitionFit: Ballistic describes the motion of objects thrown or fired, so projectile as an adjective.

entries.clue: Foolish mother leaves in a manner of speaking (7)

indicatorNotes.leaves: mother leaves, so MA departs from the word

blocks.note: ma is mother
an idiomatic expression is a manner of speaking; the mother's letters sit in its middle

annotation.surface: A silly mother walks out, so to speak.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' looks like a hedging phrase; it defines IDIOMATIC.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain adjective synonym: an idiotic plan and a foolish plan are the same thing.

entries.clue: Serial killer’s second, false, nationality (7)

indicatorNotes.false: a false version is not the real arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder
the second letter of kIller

annotation.surface: A serial killer's second passport gives a false nationality.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Killer's second' looks like an accomplice; it is the second letter of killer.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Israeli is one example of a nationality, as a passport would record it.

entries.clue: Dress suggestively revealing half of girdle? (3,2)

blocks.note: the first three of the six letters of girdle
the answer only suggests its wordplay: the direction word that turns the half-girdle round in a down entry is written into it

annotation.surface: A dress is cut so as to show a glimpse of underwear.
annotation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer is itself the instruction. In a down entry, RIG going up reads GIR, half of girdle; the question mark owns up to the trick.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb: to rig someone up, like rigging them out, is to dress or kit them out.

entries.clue: Marx brother takes in Silver City (7)

indicatorNotes.takes in: to take something in is to hold it inside, so the brother's name holds the metal's symbol

blocks.note: Chico was one of the Marx Brothers
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

annotation.surface: A Marx brother goes to see a film called Silver City.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Silver City' reads as one name; the two words split, silver the wordplay and City the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Chicago, on Lake Michigan, is the third-largest city in the US.

entries.clue: Run into something with teeth — one little dog (5)

indicatorNotes.into: running into something here means going inside it, so the letter for run sits within the toothed thing

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
a cog is a toothed wheel
I is the Roman numeral one

annotation.surface: Someone runs into a creature with teeth, just a little dog.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Something with teeth' sounds like the dog itself, but it is a cog.
annotation.definitionFit: The corgi is a small short-legged dog.

entries.clue: Delivered welcome change where sacrifices maybe made (4,5)

indicatorNotes.Delivered: a speech delivered is spoken, so the words are heard rather than read

blocks.note: hi is a greeting, a welcome
to alter is to change

annotation.surface: A welcome change has been delivered.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' in the definition allows that not every high altar sees sacrifice.
annotation.definitionFit: A high altar is the main altar of a church, and altars are where sacrifices are made.

entries.clue: Giant artist missing an island (5)

indicatorNotes.missing: the artist is missing the I

blocks.note: Titian was a Venetian painter
I is the abbreviation for island; remove it from TITIAN

annotation.surface: A great painter is missing an island.
annotation.walkthrough: Either I of TITIAN may go; the second leaves TITAN.
annotation.definitionFit: A titan is a giant, from the giant gods of Greek myth.

entries.clue: New unopened iPod with plastic micro CD (10,5)

indicatorNotes.New: new letters are made from old, so the fodder is rearranged

blocks.note: iPod without its first letter
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A brand-new, still-sealed iPod comes with a plastic micro compact disc.
annotation.walkthrough: CD looks like a compact disc beside the iPod; it is the abbreviation for Corps Diplomatique, the diplomatic corps.
annotation.definitionFit: An abbreviation: CD, for the French Corps Diplomatique, appears on embassy car plates and means the body of foreign diplomats in a capital.
